newsitem.title: INDIA: India's air exports boosted by new Central Bank credit.
newsitem.headline: India's air exports boosted by new Central Bank credit.

text.p: Air cargo traffic should benefit from a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) instruction to banks that they can extend credit facilities for exporters, cargo analysts said.
Government officials said that concessional credit had only been available until now for exports linked to foreign currency projects sponsored by bodies such as the World Bank.
Now, after instructions from the Finance Ministry, any shippers of goods officially classed as exports will be able to ask banks for pre-shipment credit and post supply credit.

The concession period would be for a maximum period of 30 days or up to the actual date of payment by the receiver of goods whichever is earlier. The RBI would cover bank financing at pre-shipment and post supply stages, the officials added.

Cargo analysts said this would give exporters more leeway to meet demand and allow them respond to orders much faster. The air cargo industry would be a prime candidate for these concessions enabling it to reduce payment risk and relieve bottlenecks. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
